facts.fact: Global Voices, citing Gabon Review, says a law enacted on 5 October 2026 ratifies the social media ordinance and establishes a regulatory framework for AI-generated and AI-amplified content.
facts.system: Law ratifying the social media ordinance (AI-generated and AI-amplified content)

GAB.note: The document names an identification requirement for social media users but states no data protection law, authority or decision.
The 1.84 million figure counts people denied platform access, not people who use the internet.

facts.fact: Global Voices reports that on 17 February 2026 Gabon's media regulator HAC suspended Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube until further notice, and lifted the suspension on 24 October 2026 after 248 days.
facts.system: HAC suspension of social media networks

GAB.note: The document names no local research institution.
